scope: Long-tail handheld, vintage-computer, multi-title runtime, and software-system projects, verified against maintainer repositories and deduplicated against the live SQLite catalog plus reviewed research batches.

projects.title: ALIS: Silmarils Virtual Machine Reimplementation
projects.platform: Multiple original Silmarils releases (PC, Atari ST, Amiga, Macintosh, and others) → Windows, macOS, and Linux; input-version support varies by title
projects.status: In development; the maintainer's compatibility table marks multiple games playable for PC, Atari ST, and Amiga versions, while some other source versions are unknown or not working. The README lists Windows, macOS, and Ubuntu builds/tests; users supply original game data.
projects.summary: A reverse-engineered reimplementation of Silmarils' ALIS (Actor Language Integrated System) virtual machine. It interprets original game data and scripts with reconstructed VM opcodes and platform services; it is not a matching decompilation or a general-purpose system emulator.
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source; original game data files must be supplied by the user

projects.title: Azel: Panzer Dragoon Saga Reverse-Engineered PC Runtime
projects.status: Early native Windows reimplementation; the maintainer says the beginning of the game is semi-playable, with bugs, through the Arachnoth battle. The user must provide the contents of disc 1; no release package is listed.
projects.summary: A C++ reverse-engineered reconstruction of Panzer Dragoon Saga for Windows. The README describes an early playable portion rather than a matching Saturn decompilation; game data is read from the user's disc and is not part of the repository.
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed C++ source; requires user-provided content from the first Saturn disc
projects.subtype: Sega Saturn reverse engineering and Windows runtime

projects.title: OpenCaptive: Captive Reimplementation
projects.platform: DOS game data (with Amiga and Atari ST data analysis) → Windows x64, Linux x86-64, macOS arm64, Android, and iOS
projects.status: Actively developed; the maintainer lists release v1.1.126 and describes a playable DOS-based compatibility runtime with verified data, combat, audio, map generation, saves, and rendering. The currently verified navigation stops at the real Mission 0001 route-selection boundary; Amiga data is verified but not yet exposed as playable, and Atari ST support is analysis-only.
projects.summary: A C/SDL3 source-faithful reimplementation of Captive. It uses hash-verified, user-supplied original files and the maintainer compares behavior with the original DOSBox-X runtime; it does not bundle the commercial game data.
projects.strategy: Source-faithful reimplementation with a DOS compatibility runtime
projects.language: English, Swedish, German, French, Spanish, Italian, and 13 additional languages
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed C source and releases; user supplies the original game data

projects.title: Celeste Classic C Source Port (ccleste)
projects.platform: PICO-8 → Windows/Linux/macOS PC, Nintendo 3DS homebrew, and an experimental WebAssembly build
projects.status: The archived repository documents working PC and 3DS builds, releases, and an experimental web port. The repository was archived by its owner on 2023-11-07; no later upstream maintenance is implied.
projects.summary: A portable C source port of Celeste Classic whose gameplay code was manually translated from the original PICO-8 Lua. The SDL frontend supports desktop hosts; a separate Makefile builds a Nintendo 3DS homebrew package. This is a source reimplementation, not a machine-code recompilation.
projects.strategy: Manual Lua-to-C gameplay reimplementation with platform frontends
projects.source_available: Public source and releases; upstream repository is archived

projects.title: NGageRecomp: Nokia N-Gage Static Recompiler Framework
projects.game: NGageRecomp static-recompilation toolchain for N-Gage software
projects.platform: Nokia N-Gage / Symbian OS 6.1 ARMv4 E32Image → native Windows, Linux, and macOS; other handheld hosts are stated targets, not verified compatibility claims
projects.status: Experimental framework; its README reports a SonicN render-loop proof that currently produces a blank/loading frame, while the separate Snakes target lifts all engine functions and reaches application initialization but not menu/gameplay. No release package is listed.
projects.summary: A static ARMv4-to-C recompiler plus a native Symbian HLE runtime for N-Gage applications. It is a multi-title development framework; game-specific targets live in separate repositories. The maintainer identifies IDA Pro 9.1 as the current analysis front-end and Ghidra 12 as a fallback/cross-check.
projects.strategy: Static ARMv4-to-C recompilation with a native Symbian HLE runtime
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source; the primary documented IDA Pro front-end is proprietary, with Ghidra noted as an alternative; users provide their own N-Gage software

projects.title: OpenClaw: Captain Claw Reimplementation
projects.platform: Windows PC → Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and browser via Emscripten/WebAssembly
projects.status: The README documents a playable Emscripten build and says the game runs on Android, although Android deployment instructions were incomplete. projects.strategy: From-scratch native game reimplementation with original data files
projects.source_available: Public GPL-3.0 source; requires the user's original CLAW.REZ game archive
projects.subtype: Multiplatform PC game reimplementation and WebAssembly port

projects.title: Rayman 3 Readvanced
projects.game: Rayman 3 (Game Boy Advance and Nokia N-Gage versions)
projects.platform: Game Boy Advance and Nokia N-Gage → Windows x64 (macOS, Linux, and Android are planned, not current supported targets)
projects.status: In development; the maintainer says there are no downloadable builds yet. Windows 7+ x64 is the only listed supported platform; GBA, N-Gage, and specified regional ROM/data variants can be supplied to the program. Future host platforms are explicitly described as planned.
projects.summary: A MonoGame/C# recreation of the GBA and N-Gage versions of Rayman 3, with original decompiled C behavior rewritten in C# rather than a byte-matching source reconstruction. It requires user-supplied game data, adds optional high-resolution and quality-of-life features, and currently has no released build.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-3.0 C# source; original GBA or N-Gage game data is required and not supplied

projects.platform: Game Boy Advance (European release with English, Japanese, French, German, Spanish, and Italian) → rebuild of the matching GBA ROM
projects.status: Work-in-progress matching decompilation; the maintainer states that it builds the European ROM identified by SHA-1 685af3a2dc0f1b3f8922e73ec42c1dc92e210e39. A matching user ROM is required; the README says no game data is included. The maintainers explicitly prohibit LLM-generated issues and pull requests.

This is a distinct title-specific project in the Sonic Advance Trilogy Research organization, separate from the Sonic Advance 1/2 repository; the source repo does not distribute the ROM.

projects.title: System 7 Portable Reimplementation
projects.platform: 68K-era Macintosh System 7 behavior → x86 BIOS/UEFI (QEMU and one tested UEFI ThinkPad); ARM/ARM64 QEMU targets are partial and PowerPC is experimental
projects.status: Active educational proof of concept. The README reports a responsive desktop under QEMU and on one physical UEFI ThinkPad; ARM64 reaches the event loop in QEMU, while PowerPC remains experimental. Small test 68K programs run, but real Apple applications and broad hardware compatibility are unverified.
projects.summary: A clean-room reimplementation of the Macintosh System 7 operating environment for modern x86 hardware, booting through GRUB2/Multiboot2. It implements a System 7-style desktop, file/resource managers, and a 68000 interpreter with Toolbox traps for test applications; it does not include Apple source code.
projects.strategy: Clean-room operating-system reimplementation informed by reverse engineering
projects.language: English by default; 38 locale resource sets are documented, with other locales selectable at build/boot
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source; the README states that no Apple source code is used
projects.subtype: Vintage operating-system reimplementation and 68K application runtime
